title: Adjoint-normalized continuous section coordinates and coefficient naturality
statement:
Let $k$ be a field with separable closure $\Omega$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with its Krull topology. Suppose the fibre products $W_q=(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega)^{q+1}_{/k}$ [def-pc-fibre-product] have been identified with the profinite test objects $\Omega[G^q]$ [def-sfb-profinite-test-objects], with cumulative vertices $x,xg_1,\ldots,xg_1\cdots g_q$. Let $A$ be any nonarchimedean normed field with its metric topology. Define $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ on profinite sets [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] and $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. There are canonical ring isomorphisms
$$\Gamma(W_q,R_{A,k})\cong C(G^q,A),\qquad \Gamma(\Omega[S],R_{A,\Omega})\cong C(S,A)$$
for every $q\geq0$ and profinite $S$. They are normalized by evaluation on the displayed geometric points, using the adjoint equations for the canonical continuous-ring comparison [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison]. In particular $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}\Omega,R_{A,\Omega})=A$. Every face or degeneracy acts on the first isomorphism by precomposition with its increment map; the base-vertex move in the zeroth face acts trivially on coefficients. For every continuous field homomorphism $\varphi:A\to B$, the coefficient morphism $p_T^*\varphi_*$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] acts in both displayed isomorphisms by $f\mapsto\varphi\circ f$, commutes with all these reindexings, and induces $\varphi$ on $q=0$ sections. Moreover $v^*R_{A,k}\cong R_{A,\Omega}$ for $v:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, compatibly as ring objects [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. Completeness and algebraic closedness of $A$ are not assumed.

proof.text: The metric topology on $A$ is Hausdorff and totally disconnected. Indeed, for distinct $a,b$, the ball $B(a,|a-b|)$ contains $a$ and excludes $b$. It is clopen: for $z$ outside that ball, the ultrametric inequality shows that $B(z,|z-a|)$ is disjoint from it. A connected subset containing both $a$ and $b$ would therefore be separated by this ball and its complement. The same argument applies to $B$ whenever a coefficient map is given. No completeness is involved.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, totally disconnected coefficient hypothesis; elementary ultrametric verification.

proof.text: Construct the affine test identification directly. For every profinite S and commutative ring R, LC(S,R) is the pushout of LC(S,Z) and R over ULift Z. A map from this pushout is the locally constant lift of the R-map and the spectral label map; ringHom_ext_of_specMap proves uniqueness. Applying Spec gives the defining pullback square of the profinite test object. This includes empty S and the zero ring. No finite-partition colimit or finite affine coproduct theorem is required.

source.place: Generic-field continuous-coefficient calculation; direct affine-test universal-property implementation using LocallyConstant.liftPrimeSpectrum and ringHom_ext_of_specMap in the adopted source library.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-prime-spectrum] with $R=\Omega$. Since $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ has one point, step 2 gives a homeomorphism $|\Omega[S]|\cong S$, whose inverse sends $s$ to the prime $\{h:h(s)=0\}$. This is precisely the label projection $\pi_S$ in [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison]: the characteristic function of each clopen subset takes values $0,1$, so its integer evaluation labels and its $\Omega$-evaluation labels select the same clopen subset. Thus the maps $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\Omega[S]$ of constant label $s$ evaluate functions at $s$. Taking $S=G^q$ also identifies $|W_q|$ with $G^q$ under the identifications assumed in the statement. This argument does not require $\Omega$ to be perfect.

proof.text: Install the ultrametric instance from the nonarchimedean norm and use total disconnectedness. The canonical comparison is an isomorphism by lem-sfb-continuous-ring-universe-realization and a ring-object morphism by def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison. Forget to presheaves of commutative monoids, evaluate, and reconstruct ordinary section rings using reconstructedRingIso of def-weil-pbc-continuous-coefficient-module-encoding. This gives a ring equivalence from the actual section ring to continuous functions, whose underlying map is exactly comparison followed by ULift.down. Precompose with the inverse label homeomorphism and the supplied e_q. Evaluation on the singleton spectrum gives point sections. The nerve already exists in the statement; no additional separable-cover theorem is used.

source.place: Example 3.1, p.6, continuous-function realization; explicit adjunction normalization of the comparison.

proof.text: For a continuous field map $\varphi:A\to B$, define $\Phi_X:F_{A,X}\to F_{B,X}$ on sections by $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h$. This is a ring-sheaf morphism because the operations are pointwise and restriction is precomposition. The coefficient map $\varphi_*$ is the postcomposition map of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]. The adjuncts of $\Phi_X\sigma_{X,A}$ and $\sigma_{X,B}p_X^*(\varphi_*)$ coincide: on $f:S\to A$ they are respectively $\varphi\circ(f\circ\pi_S)$ and $(\varphi\circ f)\circ\pi_S$, by the defining adjoint equations [def-sfb-continuous-ring-canonical-comparison]. Associativity of composition and injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection give equality of these morphisms. Evaluating this equality in the coordinates of step 4 proves postcomposition in both displayed section rings, and evaluation at the single point proves that the degree-zero map is exactly $\varphi$.

source.place: Example 3.1, p.6, functoriality in topological rings; elementary calculation of the two normalized adjuncts.

proof.text: Prove the simplex coordinate equation directly from AreCoordinates, without FieldSeparableCech.face_coordinates. The underlying scheme functor preserves these finite connected wide-pullback limits, so maps into W_n are determined by vertex projections. The Cech map selects vertex alpha(j). If h_j is the cumulative product at alpha(j), then h_0 times the product of the first j increments h_i^{-1} h_{i+1} is h_j, by induction using List.prod_take_succ. This proves every vertex equation, hence the geometric-point coordinate equation. Naturality of comparison turns restriction into precomposition. The base-vertex automorphism fixes the unique point of Spec Omega, so its action on coefficient values is trivial. The argument covers every simplex map, including all faces and degeneracies and degree zero.

source.place: Example 3.1, p.6; agent cumulative-vertex calculation in the generic-field Cech subargument of det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-direct-images proof (3).

proof.text: Apply the monoidal natural isomorphism $v^*p_k^*\cong p_\Omega^*$ of [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] to the condensed ring $\underline A$. The ring structures on the two sides are obtained by applying these strong monoidal functors to the multiplication and unit of $\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Monoidality therefore gives $v^*R_{A,k}\cong R_{A,\Omega}$ as ring objects. Naturality also makes this isomorphism commute with $\varphi_*$. Every use of a coefficient field above required only its nonarchimedean norm topology.
